lyrics:
[Intro: upright bass line alone, then triangle and a scraped gourd]

[Verse 1: warm, soulful, bass and light percussion]
Let the power go out all down the street
Let the phones go quiet in our hands
I'm alright, I'm alright
Long as you stay where I can see you

[Chorus: strings enter, voice opens]
So stay, stay
Stay where I can see you
Oh, stay
Stay where I can see you

[Verse 2: warm, a little stronger, strings underneath]
Let the river come up over the road
Let the wind take the shingles one by one
I'll be fine, I'll be fine
Long as you stay where I can see you

[Chorus: strings fuller, backing voices hum]
So stay, stay
Stay where I can see you
Oh, stay
Stay where I can see you

[String Break: strings play the melody over the bass line]

[Final Chorus: voice ad-libbing, strings and backing voices]
So stay, stay
Stay where I can see you
Whenever there's trouble, just stay
Stay where I can see you

[Outro: bass line alone again, triangle, fade]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 118 BPM, 4/4, A major. A calm, steady walk with a gentle Latin lilt in the percussion. Reassuring and dignified.

VOICE: Male, a warm baritone with a tenor's lift, soulful and smooth with a gospel background. He begins restrained and opens up in the choruses, with pleading ad-libs in the last one. Soft backing voices hum behind him.

INSTRUMENTS: An upright bass playing a short, memorable, repeating line, alone at first. A triangle and a scraped gourd (guiro) keeping time. A soft brushed snare. Acoustic guitar. A string section that enters at the first chorus, takes the melody in the break and soars at the end.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, the bass line alone, then percussion. 0:16 Verse 1. 0:44 Chorus 1, strings enter. 1:04 Verse 2. 1:32 Chorus 2. 1:52 String break. 2:12 Final chorus with ad-libs. 2:36 Outro, the bass line alone, fading by 2:48.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-1960s New York soul: warm, roomy and simple, bass and voice in front, strings lush behind.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The bass line alone in the first eight seconds.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The disasters are a power cut and silent phones, and the request is the one made to small children and to old husbands and wives. It moves the song from romance toward the long haul.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Calm, need, reassurance.
